summary: Hybrid streaming traffic billed under batch tariff causing reserve-credit depletion for BrightCart
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reported that over the last 24 hours several thousand streaming API calls (streaming=true) were charged against their reserved batch credits and consumed their burst buffer. Impact: unexpected credit depletion and provisional overage alerts.

Impact:
- ~3,200 streaming requests billed at batch microbatch rate over a 6-hour window (estimated 12% of daily reserved buffer).
- Customer-facing alerts triggered autopause on one production worker pool.
- BrightCart reported regression in forecasted spend and requested immediate correction.

Environment:
- Dedicated org: brightcart-prod
- Region: us-east-1
- Serving: dedicated pool (pool-id: dp-1019) behind edge-proxy cluster ep-us-e-3

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send streaming request with chunked transfer (Transfer-Encoding: chunked) and header X-Stream: true to /v1/chat/stream endpoint using customer's API key.
2) Observe meter records in /metrics/postback endpoint that show request_type: batch and rate_id: reserved_microbatch instead of streaming_tokens rate.
3) Check invoice preview; reserved buffer reduced accordingly.

Logs / evidence:
- Snapshot of postback event (postback-id: pb-20260310-77a) shows request_type=batch, headers trimmed: Transfer-Encoding missing.
- Edge proxy access logs show chunked requests being normalized by proxy rewrite rule stamped 2026-03-09.
- Console billing trace: billing-line: RESERVED_MICROBATCH | qty: 3200 | timestamp range 2026-03-10T02:00Z - 2026-03-10T08:00Z.
- BrightCart usage CSV attached by customer (not in ticket): shows streaming=true on client side.

Notes on customer impact: Customer is on a reserved plan with committed burst credits; consuming those unexpectedly has immediate operational impact (autopause) and financial implications (estimated $1,200 provisional overage if not reverted).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: edge-proxy normalization removed Transfer-Encoding and/or X-Stream header, leaving metering ingress to classify request as 'batch'.
2026-03-10 10:15 - Support reproduced locally by sending identical streaming request through edge-proxy; observed header rewrite.
Metering service mapping rule order: 1) content-type sniff 2) request_type header 3) transfer-encoding presence. A recent router rollout (rollout-id rtr-20260309) added an HTTP/1.1 normalization filter that strips Transfer-Encoding for chunked requests forwarded to internal metering.
Correlation found: pb-20260310-77a and other postbacks share proxy trace id ep-trace-88a.
Temporary mitigation: revert normalization filter on ep-us-e-3 cluster and redeploy config 2026-03-11 01:00 UTC.
Observed after mitigation: new streaming requests correctly classified as streaming and billed against streaming_tokens.
Open questions: why X-Stream header was not sufficient to guarantee correct classification (metering ingress priority issue).
resolution:
Hotfix applied: metering-service PR #2412 updated classification precedence to prioritize explicit X-Stream header over Transfer-Encoding presence. Edge-proxy config rollback applied to ep-us-e-3.
Customer-facing remediation: provisional credit of $1,200 applied to BrightCart's account to offset the misbilled period. Credits refunded to reserve buffer; autopause on worker pool lifted after credits applied.
Root cause: proxy normalization introduced by router rollout rtr-20260309 removed Transfer-Encoding from proxied requests and metering classified by fallback rule that treated missing header as batch. Classification precedence bug then caused X-Stream header to be ignored in some code paths.
Status: Partial fix deployed 2026-03-11 01:00 UTC, full fix merged to main and scheduled for canary 2026-03-13.
Follow-up actions: add e2e test for streaming classification, add metric alert for sudden shift in streaming/batch ratio per org, update runbook.
